newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-TRACY CHARGES TO THIRD CONSECUTIVE CART WIN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-TRACY CHARGES TO THIRD CONSECUTIVE CART WIN.

text.p: Canadian Paul Tracy charged back from a lap down to record his third consecutive victory of the season at the inaugural St Louis 300 CART race on Saturday.

Tracy, who drove a Penske Mercedes-Benz, overtook fellow Canadian Patrick Carpentier with two laps to go in the 236-lap race and crossed the line 2.391 seconds ahead of his compatriot, who drove a Reynard Mercedes-Benz.
Brazil's Gil de Ferran finished third in a Reynard Honda, followed by Alessandro Zanardi of Italy in another Reynard Honda.

With his third consecutive victory in the 17-race CART series, Tracy extended his lead in the championship with 85 points. Zanardi is second on 67 points with Scott Pruett, who walked away from a crash that demolished his car Saturday, third at 61.
"It builds a lot of confidence," Tracy said of being able to storm back to victory after falling a lap behind.
Tracy's problem came from having to pit out of sequence with the leaders early in the race, a situation that left him playing catch up for much of the day.
"We stayed in on that first stop, and that put us a lap down," he said. "I thought 'it's going to be a long race'."
He was right about it becoming a long day as the race was slowed by eight caution periods over 88 laps.
At the last restart on lap 202 the race came down to a 35-lap sprint to the finish, from which Tracy started seventh.
Tracy seemed to pick off the drivers ahead of him with ease as he closed in on his 13th career victory.
"Really, Patrick (Carpentier) was pulling away very steadily," Tracy said. "My approach was to pass Alex (Zanardi), Jimmy (Vasser) and Gil. Then we were able to make a quick short run on him."
He used the entire track to start his charge on the rookie Carpentier, whose best previous finish was ninth.
For the second successive race, Tracy took over first place when the leader had to slow to avoid running out of fuel in the closing laps.
"I didn't know he had to save fuel," Tracy said. "At the end I knew we could go for it ... we knew we had enough fuel to go to the end."
But Carpentier's Bettenhausen Motor Sports team owner, Tony Bettenhausen, was telling his rookie driver: "you've got to save fuel."
"At first I didn't want to (slow), I was leading, pushing hard," said Carpentier, who coasted to a second-place finish.
"Paul kept it flat out and I knew he was going for it."
